facts.value: Each invocation classifies the joint list for the two-point enclosing rectangle. Disabled or hidden joints are marked CollJoint_TooFar. Among enabled, visible joints, CollJoint_B10 forces eligibility regardless of geometric bounds; otherwise disjoint joints are marked too far and overlapping joints have TooFar cleared. The pass sets didCheckBounding.
facts.rationale: Preserves the baseline behavior while making the outer enabled/visible guard take precedence over B10.

evidence.why: Exact guard ordering, flag writes, completion marker, and delegation.

facts.value: Each invocation classifies the joint list for the four-point enclosing rectangle. Disabled or hidden joints are marked CollJoint_TooFar. Among enabled, visible joints, CollJoint_B10 bypasses geometric rejection; otherwise overlap clears TooFar and disjointness sets it. The pass sets didCheckBounding, and wall-query callers skip joints marked TooFar.
facts.rationale: Corrects the unqualified B10 exception while retaining the caller-consumed broad-phase state behavior.

evidence.why: Classification precedence and complete four-point wrapper.

facts.value: Begins with result false and min_dist2 = F32_MAX. It creates and later removes a segment bounding check only if no enclosing check was active. It skips too-far joints and joints rejected by the skip/only filters, then scans each accepted joint's left-wall range followed once by its dynamic range, accepting only enabled, nonempty left-wall lines. A candidate replaces all requested outputs and latches success only when its signed squared-displacement metric is strictly less than the current minimum. The function returns the success latch after conditional bounding cleanup.
facts.rationale: Corrects the baseline's infinite-distance wording to the exact source initializer while retaining the verified traversal, selection, output, and ownership behavior.

evidence.why: Complete body directly establishes every described transition.

facts.value: The floor query leaves retained collision geometry unchanged and writes only requested outputs. It follows previous or next links while the query x lies outside the current segment and the neighbor is a floor. Missing or non-floor adjacency fails beyond 0.1 units and otherwise clamps to the endpoint. Direction tracking is asymmetric: previous-link traversal sets dir=-1, but next-link traversal does not set dir=1. Thus a forward walk can reverse into a backward walk; after a backward transition, an attempted forward reversal instead clamps x to the current segment's v1 endpoint and terminates.
facts.rationale: The current body initializes dir to zero, assigns only -1, and omits a positive assignment in the successful next-link branch. This replaces the baseline's symmetric reversal-prevention claim with the actual control flow.

evidence.why: Complete floor function establishes all direction transitions, terminal checks and output writes.

facts.value: Starts with no hit and best metric F32_MAX. Reuses an active bounding scope or temporarily bounds the four edge vertices with an AABB and clears that scope on return. Applies joint culling and skip/only filters, scans ordinary right-wall then dynamic ranges, and accepts only enabled nonempty right-wall lines. Each endpoint is tested only when squared remapped-to-current displacement exceeds 0.001F. An accepted crossing replaces the result only when its signed squared-distance metric is strictly smaller.
facts.rationale: Preserves verified behavior while correcting finite initialization terminology.

evidence.why: Complete initialization, filtering, candidate ranking and cleanup.

facts.value: Reuses an active bounding scope or creates an AABB enclosing the four supplied edge vertices and clears it before return. Applies joint culling and skip/only filters, scans ordinary left-wall then dynamic ranges, and ignores disabled, empty or non-left-wall lines. Both endpoints are tested only when squared relative displacement exceeds 0.001F. Starting from F32_MAX, candidates replace the result under a strict signed squared-distance comparison. Collision geometry is not modified.
facts.rationale: Corrects threshold units and bounding shape directly from the implementation.

evidence.why: Complete left-wall state progression and squared threshold.

facts.value: Preserves an existing bounding scope. Otherwise temporarily bounds the vertical segment from (point.x, point.y) to (point.x, point.y - 30000.0F). Skips culled or excluded joints and applies the optional only-joint restriction. Scans each accepted joint's ordinary floor range followed by its dynamic range, requiring enabled, nonempty floor-classified lines. Stops at the first qualifying x-spanning line at or below the point and clears bounding state only when this call created it.
facts.rationale: Corrects the broad-phase endpoint from an absolute height to the implemented relative downward extent.

evidence.why: Exact relative endpoint, first-match traversal and conditional cleanup.

facts.value: A void-returning dispatcher with signature void (CollData* coll, int ledge_id). It treats -1 as an invalid line ID, resolves the owning joint, and invokes a non-null mpLib_JointCollisionCallback with the registered Ground context, joint index, coll, coll->x50, 3, and 0.0F.
facts.rationale: Preserves the established signature and callback argument flow while removing the incorrect non-returning characterization.

facts.value: Ignores its incoming GObj and passes no explicit arguments. It first invokes dirty-gated floor-bound maintenance over global collision state, then updates positive dynamic-attribute lifetimes. Newly expired records are removed from the active list. In the current removal implementation, head removal returns the record to the free list, whereas a found non-head record is unlinked without free-list insertion. The wrapper returns no value.
facts.rationale: Current canonical removal control flow does not support the baseline's unconditional recycling claim.

evidence.why: Floor-state inputs, cache writes, and wrapper call order.
Exact expiration and conditional recycling control flow.

facts.value: Supports environmental collision at stage corners by locating the first adjoining line beyond a forward run of left-wall lines. The returned line is not necessarily a non-wall surface: ceiling detection and left-wall resolution separately test it for ceiling classification before using it for wall-to-ceiling contact and corner handling around the environmental collision box.
facts.rationale: Preserves the demonstrated consumer role while distinguishing non-left-wall traversal from the caller's narrower ceiling requirement.

evidence.why: Left-wall corner processing consumes the result after ceiling classification.
